[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are many differences in flavor and texture between different types of seafood, which can be best appreciated through informed preparation techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] White fish like cod, halibut, and haddock have mild flavors and firm, flaky flesh.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Shellfish like shrimp, lobster, and scallops are prized for their sweet, briny flavors and tender, succulent flesh.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oily fish like salmon, mackerel, and tuna are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and have bold, distinctive flavors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Crustaceans like crab and lobster have sweet, succulent meat that is often prized for delicacy and texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To prevent overcooking seafood, use a thermometer, keep an eye on the time, cook at a lower temperature, don't overcrowd the pan, and pay attention while cooking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fresh seafood should have a mild, clean ocean smell, clear eyes, bright and shiny flesh, and a firm texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For cooking shellfish like clams and mussels, buy fresh shellfish, clean the shells, cook until the shells open, discard any that do not open, and serve immediately.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For cooking octopus, choose a fresh octopus, tenderize it, slow-cook it, monitor the cooking time, and grill or sear for texture.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Recipe for Grilled Octopus with Lemon and Olive Oil:  
- Ingredients: 1 large octopus, salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 lemon.  
- Instructions: Preheat grill, season octopus, brush with olive oil, grill for 4-5 minutes per side, squeeze lemon juice over and serve.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The taste of seafood depends on freshness, quality, and preparation, and seafood in landlocked areas can be just as good if it is fresh and properly prepared.
